rooms.who: Students on F-1 and J-1 visas in the US, and recent graduates working on OPT, a large share of them Indian. Every spring, by the April deadline, each of them must file Form 8843. Anyone who earned money must also file a nonresident return (Form 1040-NR) and usually a state return. Ordinary tax software files the wrong form (a 1040), and the fix is an amended return that the same software cannot do. Many have Social Security and Medicare tax wrongly withheld on OPT wages and must claim it back with Forms 843 and 8316. After about five years, or once on H-1B, they become tax residents and must report Indian bank accounts and mutual funds. A missed filing can hurt later visa and green-card steps.
rooms.who_pays: The student or worker pays out of pocket: a nonresident tax-filing tool each spring (federal and state fees), a service or CPA to fix a wrongly filed 1040, help with the FICA refund claim, and later a CPA for the resident-alien year and the FBAR. Some universities buy access codes to a filing tool for their students.

The buyer's procurement team sends a security questionnaire and asks for a SOC 2 report or an ISO 27001 certificate before the contract is signed, often with a date on it. rooms.who: Founders of small skincare, haircare and perfume brands in India, selling on their own site, Amazon, Nykaa and quick-commerce apps. Before the first batch ships they need a cosmetics manufacturing licence (Form 32) from the state drug controller, or a loan licence (Form 32-A) through a contract manufacturer, or a CDSCO import registration for imported products. Every pack must carry Legal Metrology declarations and the brand needs a packer registration. A brand that puts plastic packaging on the market must register as a brand owner on the CPCB's EPR portal and file returns. Perfume adds flammable-goods courier rules. The dates come from the launch, the marketplace's document checks and the annual return deadlines. They gather in India's D2C founder communities, which began as WhatsApp groups. (CDSCO is India's drug and cosmetics regulator; EPR is the producer's duty to take back packaging waste.)
rooms.who_pays: The founder pays from launch capital: state licence fees and a consultant or CA to file them, the contract manufacturer's private-label minimums, label design and the compliance stack, the Legal Metrology packer registration, and the EPR registration and returns. Marketplaces enforce it by refusing listings without the documents.

rooms.who: Founders, from any country, who set up a Delaware C-corp to raise money or hire with stock options. Two dated rules catch them. The 83(b) election must be mailed within 30 days of receiving founder stock that vests; there is no extension, and missing it means tax on every vesting date. Before the first option grant, and again every 12 months or after each priced round, the company needs an independent 409A valuation, or the options are mispriced and employees face penalties. Many founders learn both from a Hacker News thread after the date has passed. (An 83(b) election tells the tax office to tax founder stock now, while it is worth little; a 409A valuation is an appraisal of the common stock that sets the option price.)
rooms.who_pays: The company pays for the 409A out of its first raise; cap-table software bundles one into a plan (free at the smallest tier). The founder pays personally for the 83(b) (a filing service, a lawyer or accountant to check it, and the tax bill if it is missed).

rooms.who: Finance and sustainability managers at listed and large private companies in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines, with power, renewables, chemicals and oil and gas firms among the first in line. Malaysia's National Sustainability Reporting Framework requires Bursa-listed issuers and large private companies to report under IFRS S1 and S2 from FY2025 in three groups, with Scope 3 deferred one year and reasonable assurance on Scope 1 and 2 planned from FY2027 for Group 1. Singapore phased in Scope 1 and 2 reporting for listed companies from 2025, keeps mandatory Scope 3 for STI constituents from 2026, and requires limited assurance from FY2029. Most have never measured emissions or written a climate-risk statement, and their lenders and buyers now ask for the same numbers. (ISSB is the global body whose standards these exchanges copy; Scope 1, 2 and 3 are the three tiers of a company's emissions.)
rooms.who_pays: The company pays: training for the finance team, emissions-accounting software, a sustainability consultant for the first report, and an assurance provider once the phase requires it. Singapore co-funds part of a first report. Lenders sometimes price loans on the numbers, which makes the CFO the buyer.
